title: Occupancy and Residency Certification — Health-Care Absences of the Borrower
content:
A borrower who leaves home for a hospital, rehabilitation center, nursing home or assisted-living facility because of physical or mental illness keeps the home as principal residence, under the Occupancy and Residency Certification product, for up to the plan's consecutive-month limit for a health-care absence.

## Opening monitoring

1. Monitoring begins only on a health-care absence notice on file for the profile whose review status is accepted and which carries the facility admission letter the plan requires as documentation. A notice that is not on file, or not accepted, or lacks that letter, opens nothing.
2. When another borrower, or the eligible non-borrowing spouse of a Non-Borrowing Spouse Household plan, still occupies the home, no monitoring is opened, because occupancy continues.
3. *No longer in force:* the clause that the absence start date is the facility admission date per the plan's absence-start basis, not the date the notice was received, is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis for dating a health-care absence.

## During monitoring

4. *No longer in force:* the clause that during monitoring a check-in is made every check-in interval of the plan counted from the absence start date, numbered by the count of check-ins of the current absence plus one, with annual notices suspended, is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis for scheduling and numbering check-ins.
5. A caregiver or relative living in the home never counts as occupancy for the absent borrower, per the plan's caregiver setting.

## Ending monitoring with the borrower's return

6. Monitoring ends with the borrower's return only on an accepted return-home notice dated before the absence limit is exceeded; the profile becomes current and the absence start date is cleared.
7. *No longer in force:* the clause that any cycle whose due date passed during the absence is due within the plan's response grace period of the return is no longer in force; it has been superseded by the current basis for the due date on a return.

## Points of judgement

| Situation on the records | Monitoring opened? |
|---|---|
| accepted notice with facility admission letter; no other borrower or eligible non-borrowing spouse in the home | the notice meets the condition for opening monitoring |
| accepted notice with facility admission letter; a co-borrower still lives in the home | no — occupancy continues |
| notice on file but not accepted | no |
| accepted notice without a facility admission letter | no |
| a caregiver or relative lives in the home while the borrower is away | the caregiver does not count as occupancy |

*Hypothetical case on the return.* A return-home notice that is accepted and dated before the absence limit is exceeded ends monitoring; the profile shows current and no absence start date. A return-home notice dated after the limit has been exceeded does not end monitoring as a return.

superseded_clauses: The absence_start_date is the facility admission date per absence_start_basis, not the date the notice was received;

During monitoring a check-in is made every health_absence_checkin_days calendar days counted from the absence_start_date, numbered by residency_msr_absence_checkins plus one, and annual notices are suspended.
and any cycle whose due date passed during the absence is due within response_grace_days of the return.
